title: Runtime Quarantine and Surge Fallback Protocol
content:
Purpose:
This is a working playbook for how on-prem/VPC private deployments should behave when the runtime experiences rapid degradation (latency spikes, KV cache corruption, or repeated OOMs). The goal is to provide a deterministic quarantine sequence and multi-tiered fallback so customer workloads remain available with predictable degradations, and operators can roll back or heal without causing broader platform instability.

Scope and assumptions:
- Applies to Private deployments (appliance and VPC-managed) and to Dedicated pools that have private control-plane connectivity.
- Assumes both runtime and control plane have health endpoints and the control plane can toggle routing policies via feature flags/TF toggles.
- Assumes Terraform modules expose: traffic-routing policy toggles, canary weights, and an emergency-hosted-fallback toggle (reserved for enterprise).
- Not a replacement for full migration guides — this is an operational protocol for incident containment and controlled fallback.

Key concepts / vocabulary:
- Quarantine mode: runtime nodes are isolated from new traffic but continue serving existing KV/cache-backed sessions while operators inspect state.
- Surge fallback tier: deterministic degraded service modes (Tier 1 local degrade, Tier 2 cross-region degrade, Tier 3 hosted API fallback).
- Shim endpoints: backward-compatible HTTP paths and header-based feature-flags used to maintain older client behavior during compatibility windows.

Trigger conditions (examples):
1) p99 tail latency > 2× SLO for 15m AND error-rate (5xx) > 1% for 5m.
2) Repeated KV checksum mismatches observed on >30% of nodes.
3) OOM kill rate > 0.5 per node per hour for N nodes in a single rack/availability zone.

Automated detection probes (what to watch):
- control-plane/health and runtime/health endpoints (HTTP 200 expected).
- KV checksum telemetry (counter), cache-hit ratio drops, kv-eviction spikes.
- Token-level latency histograms (p50/p95/p99) and long tail increase.
- Error code distribution by model and API path.

High-level containment flow (minimal safe path):
1) Alerting -> Triage: SRE on-call assesses trigger.
2) Enter Quarantine mode (via control-plane toggle): new session acceptance = off; existing connections served read-only where safe.
3) Divert new traffic to degraded tiers according to policy (see 'Fallback tiers').
4) Run read-only integrity probes and KV sanity checks.
5) If integrity checks pass, gradually reintroduce limited write traffic behind a canary weight. If not, proceed to rollback or state-repair.

Fallback tiers (ordered):
- Tier 0 (soft degrade): local runtime continues but with aggressive request throttling, longer token timeouts, and reduced batching to relieve memory pressure.
- Tier 1 (graceful degrade): route new requests to reduced-capacity mode within same private deployment (TF toggle: "reduced_capacity_mode"). Returns clear HTTP 503 with Retry-After for incompatible endpoints.
- Tier 2 (cross-region private fallback): route traffic to a warmed compatible runtime in a different region or AZ (TF toggle: "cross_region_fallback"). Requires KV/state compatibility or request-level stateless fallback.
- Tier 3 (hosted fallback): final fallback to hosted Redwood API (enterprise opt-in). This requires explicit customer consent and audit log entries. TF toggle: "hosted_fallback_enable" and control-plane policy.

Compatibility and API shims:
- Introduce a header X-RW-Compat-Version with the runtime version we intend to support during a fallback window. The control plane should rewrite or append shim headers when diverting.
- For deprecated endpoints, support a short-lived shim (example: POST /v1/chat -> POST /v1/chat-shim) that maps older payloads to new format. This avoids client-side errors during fast rollouts.
- Ensure feature gating is backward-safe: callers without the header must be routed to the lowest common denominator.

Terraform operational notes (modules + toggles):
- Module: private-routing (exposes variables: enable_quarantine, reduced_capacity_mode, cross_region_fallback, hosted_fallback_enable). Keep defaults false; toggles are applied to customer stacks via an emergency TF workspace.
- For rapid toggle flips, use remote-state locking to avoid drift. Add a small script wrapper (scripts/tf-emergency-toggle.sh) that performs: plan -> apply with auto-approve -> post-checks.
- Keep canary-weight and timeout values as variables: canary_weight (5), canary_probe_window (5m), staged_reintroduce_interval (15m).

Safe rollback sequence (if a rollout caused the degradation):
1) Stop new rollout traffic immediately (enter quarantine).
2) Revert control-plane routing described above to last-known-good runtime version using the version manifest in S3/artifacts.
3) If revert fails, target isolated node groups for immediate replacement, leave stateful shards alone until data-checks pass.
4) If rollback cannot restore healthy status in 30m, escalate to cross-region fallback and schedule full cluster drain and rebuild.

Smoke tests and commands (run from ops jump box):
- Health check: curl -f -H "X-RW-Compat-Version: 1.12" https://runtime.internal/private/health || echo "unhealthy"
- KV probe (sample): curl -X POST https://runtime.internal/private/kv-probe -d '{"probe_key":"rw-probe"}'
- Canary request: curl -H "X-RW-Canary: true" -H "X-RW-Compat-Version: 1.12" https://runtime.internal/private/generate -d '{"prompt":"probe"}'

Telemetry gating rules (suggested thresholds to auto-enact quarantine):
- p99_latency > 2× SLO for 15m -> auto-quarantine (soft).
- 5xx_rate > 2% on critical endpoints -> auto-escalate to Tier 1.
- kv-checksum-failures > 10/min aggregated -> immediate operator page.

Chaos and rehearsal plan (periodic drills):
- Monthly: run a staged chaos drill in a non-prod private cluster: simulate KV eviction spike, validate quarantine toggle and canary reintroduction.
- Quarterly: run a full cross-region fallback test with synthetic traffic and billing/telemetry validation. Document run results in the linked confluence page.

Runbook checklist for incident commander:
- [ ] Record time of first signal and trigger condition.
- [ ] Toggle enable_quarantine = true via emergency TF workspace.
- [ ] Run KV integrity probes and paste results to incident doc.
- [ ] If canary passes for 2 windows, set canary_weight += 10 and wait staged_reintroduce_interval.
- [ ] If cannot restore, enable cross_region_fallback and notify customer-facing CS.
- [ ] If hosted_fallback used, confirm KMS and data policy checks.

Post-incident remediation and follow-up:
- Create a postmortem with timeline, root cause, and remediation plan. Link to PRs and TF changes.
- If model of failure is upgrade-induced, update the upgrade checklist to include early KV coherence checks and add a pre-rollout chaos probe.

Open questions / TODOs:
- Decide exact telemetry thresholds for auto-quarantine (proposal attached but needs product sign-off).
- Add automated TF rollbacks (currently manual due to risk of state drift). Would need gating to avoid flip-flopping.
- Define a legal/customer communication template for hosted fallback.

Notes + references:
- See linked Linear issue INF-2345 for a recent case that motivated this protocol.
- Runtime PR that added X-RW-Compat headers: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1820
- Additions to TF module should live under infra/private-routing in mono-repo.

Quick contact list during incidents:
- SRE on-call: pagerduty (primary) -> Ethan Li
- Runtime lead: Priya Desai
- Platform eng: Noah Green

This is an iterative draft. Add comments inline, flag any incompatible assumptions, and volunteer to be on-call for the next simulation run.
